summary: CUBI is a $22B regional bank that entered an Aug 5, 2024 Written Agreement with the FRB Philadelphia plus a Pennsylvania state Consent Order, both citing risk-management deficiencies in digital-asset-related services, BSA/AML compliance, and OFAC compliance. The 10-K discloses the enforcement, but Mode B counter-checks find: (a) zero pre-enforcement foreshadowing of the specific BSA/AML/OFAC issues in prior CUBI filings (EDGAR FTS confirms no specific language pre-Aug-5-2024); (b) former CFO Carla Leibold exited via 'mutual general release' 102 days before the Written Agreement (April 25, 2024) and is named individually in the Chang v. CUBI securities class action (E.D. Pa., Dec 2, 2024) which explicitly links her departure to the enforcement; (c) CEO Jay Sidhu sold $11.3M of stock in 5 tranches Nov 2024 - Feb 2025, immediately post-enforcement and around the class-action filing; (d) digital-asset deposits GREW from ~$2.8B (16% of deposits) at YE23 to $3.6B (19%) at YE24 — the bank doubled down on the deposit franchise that triggered the consent order; (e) uninsured-deposit ratio jumped 30% -> 39% over the same period; (f) Q1 2025 net income collapsed 74% YoY on a $51.3M AFS securities impairment (the 2nd 'repositioning' charge in 12 months). Auditor (Deloitte) and ICFR are clean but ICFR scope does not cover BSA/compliance controls. Composite forensic profile fits a SHORT-tier name despite the surface-level positives (no going-concern, Big-4 audit, profitable, capital ratios above minimums) — the framework is detecting Mode B underdelivery, recurring 'one-time' charges, post-enforcement insider selling, and a doubling-down on the enforced-against business line.
